```text
# PR #3967: Patch: the 20-game daily cap holds under simultaneous challenges, seeks and accepts

Closes #3842

Requests sent at the same moment can no longer take an account past `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES` (20), and each one past the cap gets `409 daily_full` (R3727004).

Before this, `has_room` counted in one transaction and committed it, and the challenge, seek or game was written in a later one. So several requests could each see 19 and all go through. Now the count is taken again inside the transaction that does the write, while holding a lock on the account. I built the plan as written, with no departures.

## What changed

- **Store** (`db/store.rs`, `db/pg.rs`, `db/fake.rs`): a new `Tx::daily_lock_account`.
  - In Postgres it takes a lock under the key `'jackioh.daily:' || id` (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`). The lock ends with the transaction and needs no new table or column, so there is no migration. It follows the same pattern as the economy's `lock_account`.
  - In the fake it only records the call as `"daily.lock"`, because fake transactions already run one at a time.
- **`daily/invites.rs`**: a new `has_room_locked` takes the lock and counts again. It runs at all four places a write happens:
  - `challenge`: after the friendship re-check, before the challenge is written.
  - `accept`: after the friendship re-check, before the challenge is closed. A refusal leaves the challenge open.
  - a seek that waits: before the seek is written.
  - a seek that pairs: before the game is written. A refusal puts the claimed seek back (`reopen_seek`) and answers `daily_full`.
  
  The early `has_room` check stays as it was, so a full account is still refused before any deck is frozen or game prepared.
- **Docs**: the "Daily games" section of the server README, §9.13 ("however many arrive at once"), and `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` added to R3727004's `proven_in`. There is no new ruling, since this enforces R3727004 as written.

## Tests

- **Store contract**: `r3727004_two_sends_racing_for_the_last_daily_place_write_one`. With 19 held, a first transaction locks and counts while a second begins. The second waits for the first to commit, then counts 20 and writes nothing.
- **API**: `r3727004_a_challenge_an_accept_or_a_seek_whose_rival_took_the_last_place_is_refused` runs four cases: challenge, accept, seek that waits, seek that pairs.
  - The fake's `before_call` hook inserts one of Ada's own seeks as the lock is taken, so she is already at 20 when the recount runs.
  - Each case must answer `409 daily_full` and leave Ada at exactly 20.
  - The accept case also checks the challenge is still open; the pair case checks Cy's seek is back and no game was made.

## Proof the tests catch the bug

- I removed each of the four recounts in turn. Each time, that case failed with `left: (201, "")`, `right: (409, "daily_full")`; the file was then restored.
- Against Postgres, with `pg::daily_lock_account` changed to skip the lock, the contract case failed 3 runs out of 3 at `!second_written`. With the lock put back it passed 3 out of 3.

## Commands run (all green)

- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store daily::`: 22 passed.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily::`: 26 passed.
- `KEEP_DB=1 sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`: exit 0, 243 passed in each of 3 shards, the new Postgres case among them. I removed the container afterwards.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server`: every binary ok (1756 passed, 1 ignored; 729 passed; and so on), 0 failed. The two ignored tests were already marked that way before this change.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: "2183 rulings, 5548 proofs, … ok".
- `cargo jackioh patches check` and `cargo jackioh catalog check`: ok.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: `Internal`, so no card plays differently and no fragment is needed.
- I did not run the web tests: no web file changed.

## Decisions

- **Which lock**: an advisory lock under its own key (`jackioh.daily:`). I rejected `select … from profiles … for update`, which would also wait on every other write to the profile row, such as R1434's username claim. I also rejected reusing the economy's lock, which would make daily sends wait on pack openings.
- **Two counts**: I kept the early count as well as the locked one. Counting only inside the write would prepare a whole game for an account that is already full.

## Look at twice

- **Deadlocks**: only the three invite-writing paths take the daily lock. Each takes one lock, the caller's own, before any row lock, and takes no other advisory lock. Cancel, decline, the seek claim and the economy lock never take it, so they cannot wait on it in a cycle.
- **The fake**: `prepare_between` and `freeze_choice` open transactions of their own. They stay outside the write transaction, because nesting one inside would deadlock the fake.
- **A gap this does not close**: when someone claims a seek, that seek leaves its sender's count when the claim commits, but the game only enters the count when it is written a moment later. A request from that sender in between can count one short and reach 21. `reopen_seek` also writes back without counting. Closing this means reshaping how seeks pair, so a person should decide whether to file it as a follow-up under #3726.

# #3842: Patch: the 20-game daily cap holds under simultaneous challenges, seeks and accepts
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

A follow-up to daily games (#3727, merged in #3762), found in its review and left out of it. Part of the tracker #3726.

### What happens

A player may hold at most `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES` (20) running games, open seeks and open challenges together (R3727004). [`has_room`](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L82-L88) (`crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs:83`) counts them in one database transaction and commits it; the new challenge, seek or game is written in a later one ([lines 180](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L180), [254](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L254) and [338](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L338)). Several requests sent at the same moment each see 19, and all succeed, so a player can go past 20.

### What should happen

However many requests arrive at once, a player never holds more than `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES`; the ones past it answer `409 daily_full`.

### How to reproduce

With 19 held, send several challenge (or seek, or accept) requests in parallel. More than one succeeds, and the count goes past 20.

### Fix

Count and insert in the same transaction while holding a per-player lock, for example `select … from public.profiles where id = $1 for update` or `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, in `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`. Keep the in-memory fake (`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`) matching, and add a case to `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` that fails without it (two transactions racing for the twentieth place: one wins, one is refused).

If it needs a migration (a trigger, say), take the next free number after `0089` and register it in `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`, `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` (the test prints the checksum to pin) and both lists in `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`.

Rated hard: concurrency in the store, the Postgres store and the fake kept in step, and possibly a migration.
